newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rate 9.5 vs 10.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rate 9.5 vs 10.3 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average money market rate eased back to 9.5 percent on Monday from 10.3 percent thanks to better supply of kuna funds, dealers said.
They put settlements at 34.5 million kuna, down slightly from last Friday. The banks sought 40 million kuna but some could not meet borrowers' terms.
Call money was steady at 9.0 percent, with one fresh loan struck at 11 percent.
The price for term loans ranged between 11 percent for one-week funds to the one-month rate of 15 percent.
The weekend overnight trade totalled 2.5 million kuna as only two banks were short and one borrowed 10.1 million through a central bank's Lombard facility to square position.
The Lombard rate is 11 percent and overnight borrowings are made at one percentage point above the average daily rate.
The central bank calculated the kuna midrates for Tuesday's dealings slightly weaker at 5.4889 to the dollar and 3.5649 to the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
